Perplex

/per-PLEKS/ - rhymes with flex · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Perplex means to confuse.

The crossword's final clue perplexed the whole break room until the night janitor read it aloud and laughed.

Worked Example

The vending machine perplexed the physics department all semester: it returned exact change for every bill except twenties, which it accepted, counted aloud, and kept.

Perplex is a shade past 'puzzle': a perplexing thing doesn't just invite curiosity — it tangles your reasoning (the word literally means 'thoroughly woven'), so each explanation you try knots into the next.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

puzzle: to set a problem that invites another try

mystify: to leave someone with no explanation at all

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

clarify: to make a thing plain

orient: to give someone their bearings

Where it sits · how far explanation slips from reach — intrigue → perplex → mystify

intrigue vs. perplex: To intrigue is milder than to perplex — curiosity is pulled, but the reasoning stays untangled.

mystify vs. perplex: Mystify goes further than perplex: a perplexing result knots your explanations, while a mystifying one leaves you without any explanation to knot.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — per-

Prefix — per-: thoroughly

Root — plex

Root — plex: woven, twisted (Latin plectere)

Put it together

Put it together: Per- (thoroughly) + plex (woven) = thoroughly woven. A perplexing problem weaves your reasons into one another until you can't pull a single thread without tightening the rest.

Use the root in a new word: complex

Use the root in a new word: complex: The recipe turned out to be complex, weaving four doughs into a single braided loaf.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral

Perplex sits between puzzle and confound: stronger than a moment's curiosity, short of total defeat. Use it when a thing tangles your reasoning — and let its unit-mates bewilder (total lostness) and confound (outright defeat) take the extremes.
